fix_commit.message: Prevent integer overflow in the ICU extension. [bugs:/forumpost/844bdd7d5c|Bug report 844bdd7d5c].
fix_commit.author: drh

findings.title: Integer overflow in icuCaseFunc16 when computing output buffer size
findings.message: In icuCaseFunc16(), the variable nOut is declared as int (32-bit signed). After calling u_strToUpper() or u_strToLower() (both returning int32_t), the result is multiplied by 2 using plain integer arithmetic: nOut = 2*u_strToUpper(...). If the ICU function returns a value close to INT_MAX/2 (approximately 1.07 billion), the multiplication overflows a signed 32-bit integer, wrapping nOut to a negative or unexpectedly small positive value. This overflowed nOut is then passed directly to sqlite3_realloc(zOutput, nOut), which accepts an int. A negative size value causes sqlite3_realloc to allocate 0 bytes (or fail), while a very small wrapped positive value allocates a far-too-small buffer. On the second loop iteration or during result storage, the actual output data is then written into this undersized buffer, potentially causing heap memory corruption.
findings.suggestion: Declare nOut as sqlite3_int64 instead of int, use 2LL* to perform 64-bit multiplication when computing the doubled output size, and replace sqlite3_realloc() with sqlite3_realloc64() so the allocation size is passed as a 64-bit value.

ground_truth.root_cause: nOut was typed as int (32-bit signed) rather than a 64-bit integer type. The expression 2*u_strToUpper(...) performs a signed 32-bit multiplication; for sufficiently large inputs the result wraps around. Additionally, sqlite3_realloc() takes an int argument, so even if nOut were computed correctly it would be truncated on a 64-bit platform unless sqlite3_realloc64() is used.
